messages.author: 0839befa8a8b7d53
messages.subject: Slow rstan extract method
parts:
The extract method in rstan has been frustrating me, as it appears to get rapidly slower as the @sim results get bigger in the stanfit object. I noticed this, because I fit a series of models in Stan and then went about simulating predictions from each. The computations bogged down in the larger models, and some investigation revealed the delay was happening inside rstan::extract.

I ended up writing my own faster extract function (see below), so worked around the problem. But if it's easy to fix it, might be worth adding to the to-do list.

Here's my special-purpose extract that performs well (but is not as flexible as extract), along with some system.time results, to see how big the delay can be.

fastx <- function( object , par ) {
    begin <- attr(object@sim[[1]][[1]],"args")$warmup + 1
    end <- attr(object@sim[[1]][[1]],"args")$iter
    object@sim[[1]][[1]][[ par ]][begin:end]
}

Timed below for extracting 5000 non-warmup samples from a single chain, for a single parameter. The model has a few thousands parameters, so a big @sim object.

> system.time( mean( fastx( fit , "mu[1]" ) ) )

   user  system elapsed 

  0.004   0.001   0.004 

> 

> system.time( mean( extract( fit , "mu[1]" , inc_warmup=FALSE ) ) )

   user  system elapsed 

  0.411   0.293   1.229

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Slow rstan extract method
parts:
Thanks for pointing this out.  In 1.0.2, it is much improved. 

For example, In a model, I have parameter real y[70, 60]:

# sf2 is a fitted object returned by function stan 
> sf2@par_dims
$y
[1] 70 60

$lp__
integer(0)

> system.time(y_34_23 <- fastx(sf2, 'y[34,23]'))
   user  system elapsed 
  0.001   0.000   0.000 
> system.time(y_34_23 <- extract(sf2, 'y[34,23]', inc_warmup = TRUE))
   user  system elapsed 
  0.000   0.001   0.001 

Note that actually sf2 has 4 chains. 

--
Jiqiang
